title: How Do Wombats Poop Cubes?
description_short:
How do wombats poop cubes? Scientists found the cube shapes already forming inside the intestine of the common wombat (Vombatus ursinus), not at the exit.

The gut wall has stiffer and softer regions. As the intestine contracts, that uneven stretch helps shape the corners, so the roughly cube-shaped droppings (with rounded corners) form before they come out.

Source: Yang et al. (2021), "Intestines of non-uniform stiffness mold the corners of wombat feces", Soft Matter 17: 475–488. DOI: 10.1039/D0SM01230K
Paper (PDF): https://hu.gatech.edu/wp-content/uploads/2021/01/Hu21-wombat.pdf

Original illustrations (simplified diagrams, not footage from the study). Synthetic voice and AI-generated music.

PubMed 33289747 (abstract): alternating stiff and soft regions; corners from faster contraction of stiff regions and slower movement at the centre of soft regions
University of Tasmania news, 2021-01-28: cubes form within the last ~17% of the intestine; two stiff and two more flexible regions around the circumference
